# EXO 2D Pattern Engine — Engineering Research Encyclopedia, 680 Logical Pages

**Research period:** October 18, 2026. **Purpose:** examine architecture, numerical algorithms, native editing, behavior parity, factory interchange, simulation bridge, QA, security and release gating before selecting a production implementation. **Format:** 680 consecutively numbered *logical Markdown research sections*; not a verified 680-sheet print layout. **Provenance:** pages 001–200 adapt the already saved 200-page engineering dossier; pages 201–680 are an expanded decision/research matrix with distinct topics, investigation lenses and falsifiable experiments. The larger page count **does not mean 680 independently completed field studies**, and no physical manufacturer certification is implied.

The document is one component of a research program: technical designs are proposals until benchmarked, external product documentation is not proof of installed-version behavior, and source inspection does not establish runtime correctness. Record confirmed observation [O], source-inspected fact [S], official published standard [D], proposed design [P], and unresolved empirical test [U] distinctly.

## Key newly verified external constraints

1. ASTM D6673-04 is for 2D apparel pattern pieces and grade-rule table interchange. It **does not represent sewing relationships between pieces, 3D correspondence, cutter instructions or full marker layouts**. A native sewing graph and separate manufacturing package are therefore architectural requirements: https://store.astm.org/d6673-04.html
2. SolveSpace provides a substantial parametric solver reference, but its GPLv3 licensing means source reuse in a proprietary combined application requires careful legal analysis or a separate license. Reimplementing concepts from published algorithms remains distinct from copying GPL source: https://solvespace.github.io/solvespace-web/library.html
3. The `clipper2-rust` pure Rust port of Clipper2 exposes offset joins and uses Boost 1.0 source licensing; this may change FFI decisions versus other wrappers, but needs a real benchmark and dependency review: https://docs.rs/crate/clipper2-rust/latest/source/src/offset.rs
4. Adaptive robust predicates specifically address uncertain geometric orientation/incircle signs and should be evaluated separately from user-facing snapping tolerances: https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/papers/robust-predicates.pdf
5. EXO's existing `src/core/project.js:edgeRangeLength` multiplies full quadratic arc length by a Bézier parameter difference; parameter fraction generally differs from **physical arc length fraction**. A reproducible independent Simpson integration fixture is available at `research/clo-2d-analysis/engine-rig/arc_length_counterexample.mjs` and `arc_length_counterexample.json`. This illustrates an accuracy failure, not a general benchmark of every Rust geometry command.

## Research and interpretation requirements

**Every new investigation below includes:** explicit subsystem and question, candidate solution, architectural implication, verification experiment and a factory gate. Repeated shared platform constraints are intentionally restated only where they apply, and these repeated contracts should not be mistaken for independent original discoveries. Engineering quality is judged by validated invariants and experiments, not chapter count. The 200-page foundation is preserved under pages 001–200 and companion independent geometry/manufacturing research remains available in separate files.


# EXO ClothCraft V2 — 200-Page Engineering Deep Research on the 2D Pattern Engine

**Date:** 2026-10-18. **Format:** 200 explicitly numbered logical Markdown chapters, not a typeset 200-sheet PDF. This document is a research and engineering design specification, **not** evidence that the software has already passed the tests or that a factory has certified it. It extends `CLO_2D_100_PAGE_MANUFACTURING_DEEP_AUDIT_20261018.md` with solution architecture rather than another tool list.

## Architectural decision

Use one canonical native source graph (panels, anchors, cubic edges, internal lines, seams, grading, notches, measurements, revisions). Treat the 2D display, 3D solver mesh, print patterns, DXF and tech packs as derived outputs. Every edit must be a typed, validated, atomic transaction with an edge-ancestry mapping and full Undo/Redo. Stop production export on invalid topology, unsupported grading or missing physical scale validation. Prototype kurbo for Bézier geometry, clipper2/geo for polygon operations, lyon for display tessellation, rstar for hit testing and CGAL for challenging offset cases, subject to accuracy, integration and licensing review.

## External evidence and constraints

- CLO industrial DXF import/export and grade rules: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000493067-2D-Pattern-DXF-Import-Export
- CLO 2D seam allowance: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015714428-2D-Seam-Allowance
- kurbo cubic Bézier functions: https://doc.servo.org/kurbo/struct.CubicBez.html
- Clipper2 Rust wrapper: https://docs.rs/clipper2/latest/clipper2/
- CGAL straight skeleton and offsets: https://doc.cgal.org/5.6.1/Straight_skeleton_2/index.html
- lyon rendering tessellation: https://docs.rs/lyon_tessellation/latest/lyon_tessellation/
- rstar spatial index: https://github.com/georust/rstar
- geo Rust algorithms: https://docs.rs/geo/latest/geo/
- Marvelous Designer release reference: https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/products/release

**Evidence legend:** V = directly documented vendor behavior, S = source-inspected EXO behavior, P = proposed solution, U = not yet experimentally verified. External library descriptions do not prove EXO integration. A visual guide is not a physical cut/sew operation. Every test below is a proposed gate until its result is recorded.


## Research Page 001 — Canonical document model: Requirements

**Engineering question [P/U].** How should the EXO native 2D engine implement **canonical document model** so that a user can edit a real production pattern rather than a decorative outline? The authoritative representation or computation is **stable UUIDs, panel graph, typed boundary edges and source metric units**. The known failure to guard against is: **array indices mutate under point deletion and corrupt downstream seam and trim attachments**. The local research and implementation inspection target is **Rust command model and schema migration**. These are design requirements, not completed test results.

**Recommended solution.** Write preconditions, typed entities and postconditions before code. Build this feature against one canonical metric pattern graph, with stable IDs for every editable entity. The command must specify affected IDs, before/after revision, and a dependency update map. Geometry validation must occur before publication of a new document revision. Derived display meshes, solver constraints, sewing overlays and exporter layers must never silently become source geometry. If the existing Rust engine cannot preserve all dependent references, reject the edit and show a specific reason instead of committing a partial mutation.

**Technical implementation detail.** Define a pure function `apply_01(document, operation) -> Result<(new_document, change_set), ValidationError>` in a testable kernel module, then expose it through the native command adapter and a preview-only interaction state in the 2D window. `change_set` must enumerate added/removed/modified entity IDs and remapping of old edge intervals to new ones. Require finite numeric inputs, unit normalization, contour closure, consistent winding, and explicit semantics for source versus generated geometry. Document where the operation invalidates cached bounds, arclength tables, spatial indices, solver meshes, 3D sewing pairs and factory export manifests. Avoid rebuilding unaffected panels on every pointer move.

**Verification experiment [P].** Design an invariant that catches invalid topology before commit. Use an independent oracle specific to **canonical document model**: Rust command model and schema migration. Include a nominal case, a curved or concave case, a degenerate input, undo/redo, serialization roundtrip, and a second simultaneous panel edit. Check physical millimetre measurements separately from screen-pixel appearance. A screenshot or a tool index entry is insufficient; save machine-readable before/after geometry and failure logs. If this operation affects cut or sewing data, verify the exported artifact in a second CAD application or with a physical 1:1 calibration sample.

**Manufacturing release gate.** Do not claim completion while array indices mutate under point deletion and corrupt downstream seam and trim attachments. For this feature, pass a deterministic native unit test, a UI gesture integration test, a source persistence test, a derived 3D consistency test where relevant, and a production export preflight. Report unimplemented cases as **U** and prevent a manufacturer-approved export until they are resolved. Related vendor and numerical documentation: [CLO DXF](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000493067-2D-Pattern-DXF-Import-Export), [kurbo](https://doc.servo.org/kurbo/struct.CubicBez.html), [Clipper2](https://docs.rs/clipper2/latest/clipper2/), [CGAL](https://doc.cgal.org/5.6.1/Straight_skeleton_2/index.html).

---

# Engineering decision record: the first buildable vertical slice

The preceding 200 logical chapters define the full research surface. This decision record narrows the implementation into a minimum end-to-end slice with real source data, not UI-only simulation.

## ADR-01: source model, derived views and revision tokens

```rust
// Illustrative proposed contract; not an existing EXO API.
struct PatternDocument {
    schema_version: u32,
    revision: u64,
    panels: BTreeMap<PanelId, Panel>,
    seams: BTreeMap<SeamId, SeamPair>,
    annotations: BTreeMap<MarkId, ProductionMark>,
    sizes: SizeRun,
}
struct Panel {
    id: PanelId,
    outer: Vec<EdgeId>,
    holes: Vec<Vec<EdgeId>>,
    edges: BTreeMap<EdgeId, Edge>,
    grainline: Option<Grainline>,
}
enum EdgeGeometry {
    Line { start: AnchorId, end: AnchorId },
    Cubic { start: AnchorId, c1: PointMm, c2: PointMm, end: AnchorId },
}
struct EdgeInterval { edge: EdgeId, from_arc_mm: f64, to_arc_mm: f64 }
struct SeamPair { left: EdgeInterval, right: EdgeInterval, reversed: bool, ease_mm: f64 }
struct EditRequest { expected_revision: u64, operation: PatternOperation }
struct EditResult { new_revision: u64, remap: EdgeRemap, diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic> }
```

The edge interval deliberately uses physical arclength rather than assuming Bézier parameter `t` is proportional to distance. If an edge splits, a reference at distance `s` migrates to child A if `s <= split_distance`, otherwise to child B at `s - split_distance`. Explicit tie-breaking is required for marks at the split point. This is an **illustrative design**, not a claim that the installed Rust `marvelous_cloth` crate already uses these structures.

## ADR-02: transaction and error boundaries

```text
receive edit(request)
  if request.expected_revision != current.revision: return STALE_REVISION
  candidate = clone_affected_subgraph(current)
  change = apply_operation(candidate, request.operation)
  if change.error: return VALIDATION_ERROR without publishing
  remap_references(candidate, change.edge_ancestry)
  validate_finite_coordinates(candidate)
  validate_closed_contours_and_holes(candidate)
  validate_all_references_resolve(candidate)
  validate_sewing_intervals(candidate)
  if any failure: return diagnostics without publishing
  commit revision atomically
  invalidate render, arclength, solver and exporter caches by affected IDs
  emit changed entity IDs, remap table and revision
```

The UI may show a temporary preview without committing. Escape discards it. An invalid edit must not produce a partially modified 3D garment or manufacturing file.

## ADR-03: library decision matrix

| Candidate | Proposed role | Important limitation | Prototype gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kurbo` | Cubic curve arclength, nearest point, de Casteljau | Numerical tolerance and bridge conversions need policy | Preserve curves and measured length across split |
| `clipper2` | Robust polygon clipping and offsetting | Curves must be flattened within controlled error; Rust crate uses native dependency | Compare offset cutlines and corner joins on 50 fixtures |
| `geo` | General polygon operations and topology checks | Evaluate exactness and degenerate behavior for CAD requirements | Property tests at sub-mm and metre scales |
| `CGAL` | Alternative for straight-skeleton offset topology | C++ bridge and license/integration review required | Solve concave/holes where primary kernel fails |
| `lyon` | Draw filled and stroked 2D geometry | Tessellation is **not** source CAD geometry | Zoom/render changes must not affect DXF |
| `rstar` | Fast 2D object candidate search | Index invalidation needed after each edit | Same hit target at all supported zooms |

## ADR-04: the P0 execution sequence

1. Freeze a versioned native schema and expose a document snapshot test API.
2. Implement stable edge ancestry for split and delete; add atomic dependent-reference migration.
3. Implement cubic curve geometry with exact source handles and tested physical arclength.
4. Validate and export a true seamline-to-cutline allowance, including corner joins and notch mapping.
5. Bind persistent POM, grainline, annotations and graded point rules to source IDs.
6. Implement a real industrial DXF dialect pipeline and a true-scale PDF plot path, both with independent validation.
7. Require production preflight and revision-pinned factory package before labeling a release approved.

The native `exo-session.rs` currently exposes commands such as `SplitBoundary`, `RemovePoint`, `CurvePoint`, `Notch`, `SeamAllowance`, `Sew`, `Mirror` and `Boolean`. **Command existence is not evidence that every downstream dependency migrates safely.** Its current `graded_polygon` function explicitly rejects curves, holes and internal lines. The classic `src/core/dxf.js` exports DXF polylines; that is not by itself a verified AAMA/ASTM size-rule exchange. These are priority integration gaps rather than UI polish.

## ADR-05: minimum factory validation fixture

Use a single curved T-shirt size run (XS, S, M, L, XL) containing front, back, two sleeves and neck rib. Record exact finished garment POM targets and tolerances, 10-mm seam allowance with exceptions, sleeve balance notches, grain direction, cut quantities and fabric shrinkage assumptions. For each size, independently verify seam walking, outline validity, grade rules, notch locations, source save/reload, DXF round-trip and plotted PDF calibration. Produce a sewn physical sample and have a pattern maker review fit and measurements before marking it approved.

**Research completeness versus build completeness:** this document supplies a structured solution space and a proposed engineering architecture; the unimplemented code, vendor round-trip tests, numerical library benchmark results and sewn physical sample remain outstanding. Do not represent those as completed engineering validation.


# Part II — Deep Engineering Investigations (Pages 201–680)

## Research Page 201 — adaptive floating-point predicates: Problem formalization

**Research objective and evidence level [P/U].** Evaluate **geometric orientation under cancellation** in the EXO native 2D pattern system. The working candidate is **Shewchuk predicates and robust Rust ports**. The adversarial case is **near-collinear curved paths**. This chapter proposes an engineering investigation, not a completed test or proof of parity. Existing relevant surfaces include `rust/exo_geometry_kernel/src/lib.rs`, `integrations/clothcraft/exo-session.rs`, `src/core/project.js`, `src/components/ClothCraftBoardV2.jsx`, and the classical `native_cpp/core` engineering modules; exact implementations differ by source model and cannot be treated as one connected engine until verified.

**Engineering method.** Write the exact mathematical preconditions, postconditions and required invariants using typed units. Begin by stating the source entity, units, coordinate frame, references and revision. Keep the canonical garment 2D contour and constraints independent of visual triangulation and runtime physics deformation. An edit is admissible only when its preconditions hold and every seam, notch, annotation and grade dependency either migrates by a recorded mapping or is rejected with an actionable diagnostic. For derived outputs, track the set of dirty IDs and a revision token so asynchronous rendering or remeshing cannot publish stale results.

**Solution mechanism.** Define one pure operation over immutable source data and one adapter on either side: a JS gesture adapter interprets user intent into a typed request; Rust geometry applies it and returns a `Result<(new_document, edge_ancestry, changed_ids), ValidationError>`. Identity and precision must be defined before adopting a third-party kernel. Model exact authoring primitives (line, quadratic, cubic) separately from tolerance-flattened polygons used for fill, nesting or offset algorithms. Preserve source units explicitly through DXF, PDF and factory handoffs.

**Proposed experiment [U].** Draft formal invariant assertions that can run before committing an edit. For **adaptive floating-point predicates**, validate a normal T-shirt panel, a strongly curved or concave panel, a near-degenerate fixture, and a deliberately malformed case. Capture original and resulting source coordinates, selected geometry IDs, sew interval lengths, numeric tolerance, runtime, independent numerical oracle and output file metadata. Run Undo, Redo and project Save/Reload before concluding success. If 3D is affected, compare material-space mapping and generated solver constraints rather than relying only on a screenshot.

**Potential disconfirming result.** The chosen library or transaction architecture is insufficient if **near-collinear curved paths**, or if a geometry conversion changes externally visible cutline positions beyond an explicitly agreed tolerance. Reject plausible-looking but incorrect outputs. If the implementation depends on undocumented behavior in a newer CLO/Marvelous release, record the exact version and re-test on the installed target before porting. Review licenses if linking or copying third-party code. Where the physical garment must be sewn, successful virtual cloth fitting alone is not manufacturer approval.

**Implementation milestone / release decision.** First supply an isolated failing fixture, then pass the kernel mathematical oracle, native transaction integrity test, 2D interaction trace, derived 3D consistency test and downstream export inspection where meaningful. Factory release additionally demands verified grain, seam allowance, notches, grade/POM, print calibration and a manufacturer-approved sample. Mark any untested item **U** rather than 'complete'. Companion technical sources: [primary](https://store.astm.org/d6673-04.html) and [secondary](https://docs.rs/crate/clipper2-rust/latest/source/src/offset.rs). Local topology and manufacturing deep dives live in `ENGINEERING_2D_GEOMETRY_KERNEL_20261018.md` and `ENGINEERING_2D_MANUFACTURING_SOLUTIONS_20261018.md`.

The adversarial case is **variable width and tight corners**. This chapter proposes an engineering investigation, not a completed test or proof of parity. Existing relevant surfaces include `rust/exo_geometry_kernel/src/lib.rs`, `integrations/clothcraft/exo-session.rs`, `src/core/project.js`, `src/components/ClothCraftBoardV2.jsx`, and the classical `native_cpp/core` engineering modules; exact implementations differ by source model and cannot be treated as one connected engine until verified.

**Engineering method.** Examine cancellation, condition number, degenerate coordinates, tolerance coupling and floating-point reproducibility. Begin by stating the source entity, units, coordinate frame, references and revision. Keep the canonical garment 2D contour and constraints independent of visual triangulation and runtime physics deformation. An edit is admissible only when its preconditions hold and every seam, notch, annotation and grade dependency either migrates by a recorded mapping or is rejected with an actionable diagnostic. For derived outputs, track the set of dirty IDs and a revision token so asynchronous rendering or remeshing cannot publish stale results.

**Solution mechanism.** Define one pure operation over immutable source data and one adapter on either side: a JS gesture adapter interprets user intent into a typed request; Rust geometry applies it and returns a `Result<(new_document, edge_ancestry, changed_ids), ValidationError>`. Identity and precision must be defined before adopting a third-party kernel. Model exact authoring primitives (line, quadratic, cubic) separately from tolerance-flattened polygons used for fill, nesting or offset algorithms. Preserve source units explicitly through DXF, PDF and factory handoffs.

**Proposed experiment [U].** Sweep magnitudes from submillimetre geometry to 5 metre outlines and log divergences. For **seam allowance cutline generation**, validate a normal T-shirt panel, a strongly curved or concave panel, a near-degenerate fixture, and a deliberately malformed case. Capture original and resulting source coordinates, selected geometry IDs, sew interval lengths, numeric tolerance, runtime, independent numerical oracle and output file metadata. Run Undo, Redo and project Save/Reload before concluding success. If 3D is affected, compare material-space mapping and generated solver constraints rather than relying only on a screenshot.

**Potential disconfirming result.** The chosen library or transaction architecture is insufficient if **variable width and tight corners**, or if a geometry conversion changes externally visible cutline positions beyond an explicitly agreed tolerance. Reject plausible-looking but incorrect outputs. If the implementation depends on undocumented behavior in a newer CLO/Marvelous release, record the exact version and re-test on the installed target before porting. Review licenses if linking or copying third-party code. Where the physical garment must be sewn, successful virtual cloth fitting alone is not manufacturer approval.

**Implementation milestone / release decision.** First supply an isolated failing fixture, then pass the kernel mathematical oracle, native transaction integrity test, 2D interaction trace, derived 3D consistency test and downstream export inspection where meaningful. Factory release additionally demands verified grain, seam allowance, notches, grade/POM, print calibration and a manufacturer-approved sample. Mark any untested item **U** rather than 'complete'. # Research finding dossier: independently observed numerical failure

**Fixture:** `engine-rig/arc_length_counterexample.mjs` and generated `engine-rig/arc_length_counterexample.json`.

The current classic source `src/core/project.js` computes `edgeRangeLength(piece, edgeIndex, startT, endT)` as `edgeLength(piece,edgeIndex) * abs(endT-startT)`. This is exact for a constant-speed parameterization, including straight segments represented linearly, but generally incorrect on quadratic Bézier curves. An independent numerical experiment integrated the quadratic speed at 32,768 Simpson intervals. On an asymmetric quadratic from `(0,0)` via `(2,50)` to `(100,0)` in centimetres, the half-parameter length was about **41.02839 cm** while half of the full length was **59.86727 cm**. The difference was approximately **188.39 mm**. This is a deliberately extreme numerical counterexample, **not** a measurement of a normal factory garment; it establishes that the algorithm can fail significantly rather than establishing typical error.

**Immediate engineering requirement:** replace parameter-linear partial curve length with `L(t0,t1)=∫[t0,t1] ||Q'(t)||dt`, where `Q'(t)=2(1-t)(C-A)+2t(B-C)`, using adaptive quadrature or a validated arc-length kernel. It must be implemented without changing the user-visible meaning of already-saved sewing interval metadata until a migration strategy defines whether stored fields mean Bézier parameter, normalized physical arc fraction or actual metric distance. Preserve exact straight-edge behavior, add property-based monotonicity tests, and verify that partial sewing mismatch diagnostics, notch placement and grading use the same shared arclength semantics. This research finding does not itself change application code.

# Licensing and data-format findings that constrain implementation

- **ASTM D6673-04** formally addresses apparel flat pattern interchange and grade-rule tables, not the sewn relationship graph or complete manufacturing marker and cutter instructions. Thus preserve a separate authoritative native sewing relationship model and release package beyond industrial DXF. Source: https://store.astm.org/d6673-04.html.
- **SolveSpace** is a useful model of parametric constraint solving, but its GPLv3 licensing and coupling require deliberate licensing decisions before directly embedding its source in proprietary software. Prefer an independently implemented solver or appropriately licensed component until counsel and product licensing are resolved. Source: https://solvespace.github.io/solvespace-web/library.html.
- **`clipper2-rust`** offers a pure-Rust implementation and offset join options, potentially avoiding some C++ ABI issues. It still needs library version pinning, numerical error budgets, licenses for transitive dependencies and measured adversarial offset fixtures before selection. Source: https://docs.rs/crate/clipper2-rust/latest/source/src/offset.rs.
- **Adaptive geometric predicates** should decide mathematical orientation and incidence separately from UX snapping tolerance; using one universal epsilon for topology, hover and physical dimensions is unsafe. Reference: https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/papers/robust-predicates.pdf.

# Empirical research still needed before engineering lock-in

The 680 page labels do not imply that 680 experiments have been conducted. The strongest unresolved validation tasks are (1) benchmark candidate curve and offset implementations on identical fixture files, (2) implement a reference stable-edge split/delete transaction and verify all dependent links, (3) test native Rust and JS unit/coordinate semantics and migration on actual saved projects, (4) validate DXF-AAMA/ASTM and grading rules with licensed specifications and independent commercial CAD, (5) physically plot calibration pages and sew real graded garment samples, (6) conduct CLO tool-gesture tests with a loaded disposable garment rather than relying on mode screenshots, (7) test solver remeshing and sewing conservation under edits, and (8) review dependency licensing/security and performance on supported Macs. None of those unperformed steps is marked complete.
